mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the prior month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened financial conditions.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05) occurs during FEDFUNDS increases exceeding 0.25% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 2% month-over-month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as strong hiring signals economic resilience.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive 5-day windows with PAYEMS > +2%, no statistically significant positive returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of 10% or more predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as it indicates cooling housing demand and reduced consumer spending momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month's value * 0.9 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period, no 60-day window shows negative returns when HOUST declines by ≥10% consecutively.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 5% from the prior quarter, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to reduced manufacturing activity and investor risk aversion.
failure_condition: In 10 such INDPRO contractions, less than 40% of predicted negative returns materialize (cumulative IC < 0.4).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over 60 days as lower unemployment supports stronger consumer demand.
failure_condition: During such UNRATE periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the risk-free rate (Sharpe ratio < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% each month for two consecutive months drive a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to dual demand signals.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month + 2% AND RSAFS > previous month + 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 50 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 1% in a single month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to inflationary pressure eroding equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 10 such CPI spikes, no negative returns occur in >70% of windows (IC > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side shock (evidenced by a one-time drop in GDPC1 of ≥5% from trend) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as market adjusts to perceived output shortfall.
failure_condition: In 20 such shocks, less than 30% produce negative 5-day returns (IC > 0.7).
